newsitem.title: USA: Margins on international power deals seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Margins on international power deals seen falling.

text.p: The heady days of high double-digit returns on international electric power projects are gone, according to a pioneer in the international power business said, replaced by returns in the mid-teens that are forcing independent developers out in favor of major oil and trading companies.

"The oil companies, if they want to play and they want to use their balance sheet as bludgeons, I think they are going to win," said John Wing, founder of The Wing Group and a former Enron Corp executive.

Independent developers are scrambling for new projects as oil companies seeking to monetize reserves and trading firms with financial clout elbow their way into major projects put up for bid, Wing said at the Cambridge Energy Research Associates annual energy forum, which ends on Wednesday.
"The business is going to be in the third world," said Wing, a former chairman of Enron Power Corp who led the effort to develop the 1,825 megawatt Teeside power project in the United Kingdom.
Instead of returns as high as 55 percent on one of Wing's early international ventures, he now sees international power projects generating profit margins in the mid-teens, he said.
"The returns are going to be dramatically lower than they were in the 1980s. I think they are going to be in the teens, and to get that you are going to have to take some risk," Wing said.

Wing recently teamed up with Merrill International Inc and DuPont Co subsidiary Conoco, on a Colombia power project, and has approval to manage two of Pakistan's seven electricity distribution companies.
